title: Release thermostat + backpressure journal
content:
Quick note log / scratchpad for the idea of a release thermostat and explicit backpressure/decay windows. This is messy — notes to self and potentially for Marco/Priya to pull into a short RFC later.

Why this?
- We keep seeing oscillations when we do quick traffic increases: latency spikes -> circuit trips -> traffic shift -> cold caches -> more spikes. Need a small control loop (thermostat) plus a decay window to smooth weight changes.
- Goals: keep p95 latency under customer SLOs during gradual ramp, avoid cascading rollbacks, enable safe automated ramps for minor version bumps.

Core concepts (working naming):
- Thermostat: automated controller that adjusts target traffic weight based on observed telemetry (latency, error rate, GPU queue length).
- Decay window: minimum time to wait before adjusting traffic downward beyond X% (prevents rapid down-and-up flapping).
- Backpressure signal: immediate caps when a strong signal (OOMs, overloaded GPUs, sustained queue length) is observed; this temporarily forces traffic away from variant.
- Gentle warmup: small pinned seed cohorts for cache warming and KV warm start before visible traffic.

Metrics and signals to use (initial proposal):
- Latency: p50/p90/p95/p99 (api_gateway + runtime token emit).
- Error rate: 5xxs and model outputs that match configured reject/quality flags.
- Queue depth: inference queue length on serving nodes (avg over 30s).
- GPU utilization and memory faults (quantized model memory pressure).
- Throughput/Cookies: requests per second by route and by cohort.
- Observability sanity: sample output quality metrics (if available) for A/B.

Thermostat heuristics (toy rules):
- If p95 <= target_p95 * 0.95 AND queue_depth < Q_low AND error_rate < E_low -> increase weight by +5% every 10 minutes (max step: 10%).
- If p95 between target_p95 * 0.95 and target_p95 * 1.1 -> hold weight steady (cooling phase).
- If p95 > target_p95 * 1.1 OR error_rate > E_threshold -> backpressure ON: immediately reduce weight by 30% and enter decay window of 30 min.
- If queue_depth consistently > Q_high for 2 consecutive 60s windows -> reduce weight 20% and extend decay window 45 min.
- Maximum gradual ramp: don't increase more than 25% of total traffic for the variant within 2 hours (safety cap).

Decay window behavior:
- Definition: after a weight reduction, do not increase traffic to the pre-reduction level until decay_window has elapsed AND telemetry is stable for a stability_window (e.g., 15 min).
- Rationale: prevents repeated flip-flop from transient blips.
- Example params: decay_window = 30m, stability_window = 15m. Can be tuned per route.

Warmup cohort sequence (manual/automated hybrid):
1) Seed cohort (0.5% users) pinned for short requests (snippets) to warm KV cache and confirm baseline correctness. Monitor latency and error for 10m.
2) Micro cohort (2%): allow long-ish sequences but limit tokens to X per request for first 15 minutes.
3) Gradual increases as thermostat allows.

Backpressure modes (fast paths):
- Soft backpressure: thermostat reduces future weight increases and triggers an alert. Human-in-the-loop review window.
- Hard backpressure: immediate reroute off the variant to the fallback model/region until automatic healing. This requires safe fallbacks (lower-capacity but stable models).

Operational checklist (pre-roll):
- [ ] Confirm telemetry dashboards exist for route: p95, error rate, queue depth, GPU mem faults. (Datadog queries sketched below)
- [ ] Register fallback model and ensure it is load-tested at target concurrency.
- [ ] Set default thermostat params for the route (store in rollout config).
- [ ] Notify release slack channel with target windows and on-call.
- [ ] Record pin/warmup cohorts in rollout metadata.

Quick Datadog query skeletons (notes to self):
- p95: avg(last_5m):percentile(api.request.latency_ms{route:xyz},95)
- queue depth: avg(last_1m):avg(serve.queue_depth{pool:gpu-pool-1})
- error rate: (sum(last_5m):count(status:5xx AND route:xyz) / sum(last_5m):count(route:xyz)) * 100

Example rollout timeline (for a minor model update):
T=0: seed cohort 0.5% (10 min warm), check asserts
T=10m: micro 2% (15 min), thermostat locked for 15 min
T=30m: if thermostat positive -> +5% to 7% every 10m until 25% reached or cap hit
T=2h: hold and evaluate long-tail p99 for 30m; if degradation -> hard backpressure and rollback plan B

Edge cases to consider / open questions:
- How to combine cross-route capacity effects? (multiple routes share GPU pool) -> we need pool-level thermostat that aggregates signals.
- Interaction with KV prefix caching: warmup cohorts may appear cheap but trigger heavy prefix cache population; warmup windows should account for extra memory churn.
- How does thermostat interact with dedicated vs hosted vs private? Private deployments may need local tuning and may prefer human gating.
- Should decay_window be proportional to magnitude of reduction? (bigger cut -> longer decay) — seems sensible.
- Can we emit a single scalar health score to make thermostat decision more robust (composite of normalized metrics)?

Mini runbook: immediate actions if thermostat trips to backpressure during a public roll:
1) Alert on-call and release lead via Slack + pager.
2) If soft backpressure: pause further increases, annotate rollout and wait 15m. If metrics recover -> resume with smaller steps.
3) If hard backpressure: immediately switch variant routing to fallback, mark incident, collect triage logs (top traces, top prompts).
4) Kick off warmup of fallback capacity if needed.
5) If rollback required, follow release rollback checklist (tagged in Confluence).

Notes and heuristics (scribbles):
- Use small step sizes early when model architecture change touches memory patterns (quantization changes, new attention kernels).
- Prefer more conservative settings for routes serving high-frequency short queries (low tolerance for p95 spikes).
- Add a flag to the rollout config: allow_thermostat_autoscaling: true/false so SRE can opt-out for manual-only flows.
- Consider an automated suggestion engine (later) that recommends thermostat params from historical rollouts.

Action items (next):
- [ ] Draft a short RFC with diagrams (thermostat control loop, decay window). Target: next release cadence meeting.
- [ ] Marco to prototype control loop in sandbox (simulate queue depth spikes).
- [ ] Priya to list necessary Datadog dashboards + log sample queries.
- [ ] I will sketch a minimal rollout config JSON for the console and dedicated router.

Random brain-dump ideas:
- Could use exponential backoff for weight increases instead of linear when traffic is large.
- When multiple variants compete for same pool, allocate a share budget and thermostat regulates each share.
- Offer a "cooldown tax" on weight increases that decays over time if previous rollouts were unstable.

End of scratchpad — intended to be ephemeral. Pull into RFC and prototype bits if we get consensus.
